h1:
Khao Yai Flower Gardens
The Bloom + Seasonal Fields
intro: Khao Yai's flower gardens are the reason a lot of people make the drive up to Pak Chong toward the end of the year — the air turns cool, there's a nice breeze, and you get to walk through fields of bright flowers laid out in neat beds with mountains in the background. The one everyone talks about is The Bloom by TV Pool, a flower field spread over 100 rai (around 16 hectares). But there are several other gardens around Khao Yai to suit different styles, so we've rounded up the ones actually open right now, along with bloom seasons, entry fees and photo spots, all in one place.

blocks.html: Pak Chong and Khao Yai sit at altitude, so from late rainy season into early winter the weather runs cooler than the lowlands. Once winter proper arrives, the gardens along Thanarat Road and over toward Wang Nam Khiao all come into bloom together, turning into fields of pink, yellow, purple and white set against the mountains — a magnet for photo-takers from November to February. Before you plan which garden to hit, here's the quick overview, because each one has a different feel.

blocks.text: The Bloom by TV Pool — the biggest flower fields

blocks.html: The Bloom by TV Pool is a large-scale flower garden covering more than 100 rai (about 16 hectares), arranged into multiple flower zones, with a 360-degree viewpoint where you can take in the wide fields against the mountains. The spots people photograph most are the big props — a giant handbag, a windmill and flower arches. The garden really is big; walking the whole thing can take an hour or more, so comfortable shoes are a good idea since a lot of the paths are dirt and grass.

items: Address — 357 Moo 5, Phaya Yen, Pak Chong, Nakhon Ratchasima
Opening hours — roughly 08:00–20:00 (open late, so you can shoot the evening lights)
Entry fee — around 100 THB for adults on weekdays and around 200 THB on weekends/holidays (part of it can sometimes be redeemed for food or drinks)
Time needed — about 1–2 hours to walk and photograph the whole field
Highlights — large fields, a 360-degree viewpoint, giant props and mountain-view photo angles

blocks.title: Check whether the flowers are actually blooming before you go
blocks.html: Flower gardens are living things — the flowers are rotated and replanted in cycles, so at certain times a garden is mid-change and the fields aren't full yet. It's worth checking the latest photos on the garden's page or calling ahead before you set off, so you don't end up disappointed — especially if you're driving a long way just to shoot fields in full bloom.

blocks.text: Hokkaido Flower Park — Japanese-garden feel near the park entrance

blocks.html: Hokkaido Flower Park Khaoyai sits on Thanarat Road around the 16 km mark in Mu Si, about 7 km before the Khao Yai National Park checkpoint. It's laid out in a Japanese style, with flowers planted in tiered beds and mountains as a backdrop, plus a Japanese-house cafe and yukata rental for photos. The grounds have grown to nearly 50 rai (around 8 hectares), with several zones alternating in colour — a good stop on the way up to Khao Yai.

items: Address — Thanarat Road km 16, Mu Si, Pak Chong, Nakhon Ratchasima
Entry fee — adults around 120–150 THB, children 6–12 around 50 THB, under 6 free (part of the ticket can be redeemed for drinks/snacks)
Highlights — Japanese-style garden, tiered flower beds, a Japanese-house cafe and yukata rental for photos

blocks.text: Floryday — European-style garden in pastel tones

blocks.html: Floryday Khaoyai is a flower-garden cafe leaning into a European look in soft pastel tones, with flower beds, photo-prop corners, a windmill, swings and viewpoints. At certain times they also rent out hanbok for photos. It suits people who prefer sweet, pretty corners over wide, rugged fields. Entry runs around 100 THB and it's open roughly 09:00–18:00.

items.name: Cosmos & sunn-hemp fields
items.blurb: In winter many gardens plant pink cosmos and yellow sunn hemp, making wide fields that photograph beautifully against the sky and mountains.

items.name: Arches & photo props
items.blurb: Almost every garden has flower arches, windmills, swings and big props, so you can get shots that don't rely on the flowers alone.

items.name: Mountain viewpoints
items.blurb: Gardens around Thanarat and Wang Nam Khiao sit at altitude, and many have spots where you can see the flower fields with distant mountains behind.

blocks.text: When do the flowers bloom best

blocks.html: The Khao Yai flower gardens are a seasonal thing. The prettiest stretch — and the most worth the drive — is winter, roughly late November through February: cool air, gentle sun, and winter flowers like cosmos and sunn hemp blooming across the fields. Outside that season the gardens stay open, but the beds may not be as full, and some are between planting cycles — so always check the latest photos before you go.

items: Nov–Feb — the prime time for flower gardens: cool air, winter flowers in full bloom, and the biggest crowds
Time of day — early at opening (soft light, fewer people) and late afternoon toward dusk (golden hour) photograph better than midday when the sun is harsh
Long weekends — very crowded, parking fills fast, and people end up in your shots; if you can avoid it, a weekday is far more relaxed

blocks.title: Drive up to Khao Yai slowly
blocks.html: Thanarat Road and the route up to Khao Yai have plenty of curves and steep stretches, and some sections get morning fog — drive slowly and leave enough distance. · Inside Khao Yai National Park, watch for wildlife crossing the road, such as monkeys and barking deer, and keep your speed down per the signs. · On long weekends traffic backs up and accommodation fills fast, so book your stay ahead.

blocks.text: Pairing your flower-garden visit with more to do

items: Comfortable walking shoes — the paths through the fields are dirt and grass and uneven in places, so sneakers or shoes you can walk easily in beat heels
Sun protection & a hat — there's little shade out in the fields and the midday sun is strong, so bring a hat, sunscreen and water
Go early — fewer people, nicer light and not yet hot, so it's easier to get your shots

Allow travel time — the gardens are spread across different zones, on both the Thanarat side and the Wang Nam Khiao side, so if you plan to hit several, map your route by the pins so you don't double back

blocks.text: Where to head next after the gardens

blocks.html: Most flower gardens take about 1–2 hours, so people like to pair them with nearby spots along the same route to fill out the day. On the Thanarat side there are European-style villages like Primo Piazza and Palio to wander and photograph. For animal farms there's Sheep Land and Farm Chokchai, and if you're after full-on nature you can carry on up to Khao Yai National Park.

items.name: Primo Piazza
items.blurb: An Italian-style village with a farm of sheep, horses and alpacas you can feed, plus European photo corners.

items.name: Sheep Land
items.blurb: A sheep farm with mountain views where you can feed the sheep and photograph the wide fields — great with kids.

items.name: Khao Yai National Park
items.blurb: Full-on nature: waterfalls, viewpoints and hiking trails that can fill a whole day.

faq.q: Which is the biggest flower garden in Khao Yai?
faq.a: The Bloom by TV Pool is the largest flower field, covering more than 100 rai (about 16 hectares), with several flower zones, a 360-degree viewpoint and big props to photograph. It's in Phaya Yen, Pak Chong, and opens roughly 08:00–20:00.

faq.q: How much is entry to the Khao Yai flower gardens?
faq.a: Prices vary by garden. At The Bloom, adults pay around 100 THB on weekdays and around 200 THB on weekends. Hokkaido Flower Park is around 120–150 THB for adults, and Floryday around 100 THB. At many gardens part of the ticket can be redeemed for food or drinks. Prices change seasonally, so check before you go.

faq.q: When is the best time to see the Khao Yai flower gardens in bloom?
faq.a: Winter, roughly late November through February, is the prettiest time — cool air, gentle sun, and winter flowers like cosmos and sunn hemp blooming across the fields. Outside that season the gardens stay open but the beds may not be as full.

faq.q: Are the Khao Yai flower gardens open every day?
faq.a: Most are open daily, though hours differ — for example The Bloom roughly 08:00–20:00, Hokkaido Flower Park roughly 07:00–18:00, and Floryday roughly 09:00–18:00. But the flowers are living and replanted in cycles, so it's best to check the latest photos on their page or call ahead before going.

faq.q: How should I prepare for a flower-garden visit?
faq.a: Wear comfortable shoes since the paths are dirt and grass, and bring a hat, sunscreen and water because there's little shade out in the fields. Go in the morning for fewer people and nicer light, and drive up the mountain slowly — the route has curves and steep grades, with fog in places and wildlife crossing the road.
